svg.title: CVE-2026-103572: how a trailing dot bypassed the Copilot config-file check
svg.desc: Untrusted text reaches Copilot. The agent asks to write .mcp.json with a trailing dot. The protected-name string check does not match, so no confirmation is shown. Win32 strips the trailing dot and the write lands on .mcp.json. A new MCP server is enabled and the IDE launches its command. Per the researcher, the fix in 17.14.42 and 18.10.4 adds a GetFullPath call that removes the trailing dot, so the check matches.
